note: agent-lifted from VB's manuals (pilot steps 2 and 3)

concepts.label: WSS attenuation drift
concepts.gloss: A degradation in which a wavelength-selective switch (WSS) gradually applies more attenuation than intended to a selected optical channel, causing low channel power.
concepts.example: A WSS set for 3 dB attenuation drifts to 7 dB, so the routed wavelength is measured at low power downstream.

concepts.label: WSS passband shift
concepts.gloss: A degradation in which a ROADM WSS passband is spectrally misaligned with a channel along its path, impairing the signal even though automatic levelling can leave its measured power normal.
concepts.example: After a ROADM adjustment, the filter centre moves off a 193.1 THz carrier; received power remains nominal but pre-FEC errors rise and OTU frame alignment may be lost.

concepts.label: WSS input port failure
concepts.gloss: A hard failure of a WSS input port that blocks every channel entering through that port while channels on other inputs remain unaffected.
concepts.example: One ROADM degree's WSS input fails, blocking all wavelengths from that degree while traffic arriving on the other degrees continues normally.

concepts.label: Transmit laser failure
synonyms: the far-end transmitter's laser has failed
concepts.gloss: A hard failure of the local or far-end transmitter laser that removes the optical signal seen by the corresponding remote receiver.
concepts.example: The far-end transponder laser turns off, causing this unit's receiver to lose its channel and raise OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: Card failure
concepts.gloss: A hard failure of a far-end equipment card that interrupts its client service and monitoring, with traffic alarms potentially masked by the equipment alarm.
concepts.example: A remote VB-OTN-LC-400 card fails, stops sending traffic and telemetry, and its equipment alarm masks derivative traffic alarms.

concepts.label: Receiver degradation
synonyms: degradation of this unit's own receiver
concepts.gloss: A degradation local to the line receiver that creates pre-FEC errors despite normal optical-path conditions and normal operation of other channels.
concepts.example: A transponder receiver develops an internal sensitivity penalty; only that receiver reports high pre-FEC BER while channel power and neighbouring channels remain normal.

concepts.label: a broken fibre
synonyms: the fibre section feeding this unit is broken
concepts.gloss: A physical break in the fibre section feeding a unit or elsewhere along a channel path that prevents optical light from traversing that section.
concepts.example: A cable cut between an inline amplifier and the receiving node leaves the downstream receiver with no light.

concepts.label: a failed amplifier
synonyms: the preceding amplifier has failed and emits no light
concepts.gloss: Failure of an optical amplifier, either the current unit or a preceding amplifier along the path, such that it emits no usable light.
concepts.example: A preceding VB-OA-ILA loses amplification and its output goes dark, causing loss of light at the next site.

concepts.label: a disconnected patch cord
synonyms: the patch cord may have been disconnected
concepts.gloss: An open optical connection caused by a removed or unseated patch cord along the channel path, particularly at a multiplex-section input.
concepts.example: A technician unplugs the patch lead feeding the preamplifier, so no light reaches the receiving end of the multiplex section.

concepts.label: a blocked ROADM port
concepts.gloss: A ROADM port state or fault that prevents a channel from passing at some point along its optical path.
concepts.example: A ROADM add/drop port is left in a blocked state, so the selected wavelength disappears beyond that node.

concepts.label: a rise in fibre loss
concepts.gloss: An abnormal increase in attenuation in a fibre section along the path, reducing delivered optical margin and potentially progressing to loss of light.
concepts.example: A damaged fibre bend adds 6 dB of loss before an amplifier, first raising pre-FEC errors and later causing an input-loss alarm.

concepts.label: a rise in an amplifier's noise
concepts.gloss: An increase in noise contributed by an optical amplifier along the channel path, reducing optical signal-to-noise ratio without necessarily removing the signal.
concepts.example: An ageing inline amplifier adds excess ASE noise, leaving channel power present but causing OTU_SD at the receiver.

concepts.label: a rise in differential group delay
concepts.gloss: An increase in polarization-dependent differential group delay along the optical path that distorts the received coherent signal.
concepts.example: A fibre event raises DGD beyond the receiver's compensation margin, producing pre-FEC errors and eventually OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: a fast polarisation transient
concepts.gloss: A rapid change in optical polarization along the path that exceeds the receiver's tracking capability and causes transient decoding errors.
concepts.example: A mechanical disturbance rotates polarization faster than the coherent receiver can track, producing a burst of errored seconds.

concepts.label: a dirty connector
concepts.gloss: Contamination on an optical connector along the channel path that introduces loss or reflection and degrades signal quality.
concepts.example: Dust on a patch-panel connector raises pre-FEC BER enough for the receiver to raise OTU_SD.

concepts.label: failure
concepts.gloss: A generic fault at a relevant card, port, switch fabric, optical channel path, or working/protection ODU path when no more specific failure class is stated.
concepts.example: PROT_ACTIVE is traced to an unspecified failure on the working ODU path rather than to a named component defect.

concepts.label: Pump or unit failure
concepts.gloss: A hard optical-amplifier failure encompassing pump-laser failure or failure of the amplifier unit itself, causing no output light and loss of carried client traffic.
concepts.example: The pump laser in a line amplifier fails, its output goes dark, and all channels through the amplifier lose service.

concepts.label: Gain loss
concepts.gloss: A degradation of an amplifier at this unit in which achieved gain falls below its target, producing weak output and a persistent OSNR penalty.
concepts.example: A line amplifier configured for 20 dB gain delivers only 17 dB, raising AMP_GAIN_OOR and weakening every outgoing channel.

concepts.label: Pump ageing
concepts.gloss: A slow incipient deterioration of this unit's amplifier pump that requires increasing drive current to maintain gain and eventually triggers an end-of-life warning.
concepts.example: Pump current rises from 100% to 121% of its beginning-of-life value while traffic remains intact, causing AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: Gain tilt
concepts.gloss: A frequency-dependent amplifier gain degradation that makes some wavelengths, typically near one band edge, weaker than others.
concepts.example: An amplifier gives 2 dB less gain to the highest-frequency channels, so only those channels arrive weak.

concepts.label: failure of this unit's pump laser
concepts.gloss: Failure of the pump laser inside the current optical-amplifier unit, preventing that unit from providing its intended optical output.
concepts.example: The pump in a VB-OA-PRE stops emitting even though input light is present, so AMP_FAIL is raised.

concepts.label: Switch fabric failure
concepts.gloss: A hard failure in an OTN switch's ODU cross-connect fabric along the path that disrupts client services and propagates ODU alarm indication signals.
concepts.example: The VB-OTNSW fabric fails, causing every ODU crossing it to carry ODU-AIS and lose client service.

concepts.label: Wrong cross-connection
concepts.gloss: An OTN provisioning error, most common after configuration changes, that cross-connects an ODU to the wrong destination without creating an optical-layer symptom.
concepts.example: After reprovisioning, ODU4 from client A is mapped to client B's egress, where ODU_TIM reports the unexpected trail trace.

concepts.label: Client port failure
synonyms: a failure of the client port
concepts.gloss: A hard hardware failure of a client-facing port at either service endpoint that interrupts the associated client service.
concepts.example: The 100GE client port at the remote endpoint fails electrically, causing CLIENT_SF for that service.

concepts.label: An impairment affecting the whole incoming line
synonyms: continues, after the node, as an impairment of each channel routed onwards
concepts.gloss: A line-wide optical impairment present on the incoming multiplexed signal that continues after the node on each channel routed onward.
concepts.example: Excess noise on an incoming ROADM degree is inherited by every wavelength switched from that degree to downstream links.

concepts.label: A power loss upstream of up to about 8 dB
concepts.gloss: An upstream attenuation event of roughly 8 dB or less that a node may re-level in power while retaining an OSNR penalty, with larger loss producing downstream low power.
concepts.example: A 6 dB span-loss increase is power-equalized at the next node, but its channels retain reduced OSNR; a still larger loss makes output power low.

concepts.label: power is normal
synonyms: does not appear downstream as low power
concepts.gloss: The affected optical channel has power within its expected range, possibly because a node has re-levelled it despite a remaining quality impairment.
concepts.example: The channel monitor reads the expected -10 dBm after the ROADM even though filter misalignment is causing pre-FEC errors.

concepts.label: the loss of signal-to-noise ratio it caused remains
synonyms: the optical signal-to-noise ratio of every channel falls as well
concepts.gloss: An OSNR or signal-to-noise degradation persists after power restoration and can make every channel carried by the affected unit noisier.
concepts.example: An amplifier restores total output power after upstream loss, but all channels remain 3 dB worse in OSNR.

concepts.label: power is low
concepts.gloss: The optical power of a particular channel is below its expected level at a downstream observation point.
concepts.example: A channel expected at -10 dBm is measured at -17 dBm after the next ROADM.

concepts.label: pass through the node unchanged
concepts.gloss: The relevant signal property or impairment is forwarded through a node without being corrected, regenerated, or otherwise altered.
concepts.example: An OSNR impairment entering a transparent ROADM remains on the wavelength leaving the node.

concepts.label: the signal arrives but is impaired
concepts.gloss: A channel remains optically present at the receiver but its quality is degraded enough to cause pre-FEC errors or, at greater severity, loss of frame alignment.
concepts.example: The receiver measures normal light but a narrowed passband raises BER until OTU_SD appears.

concepts.label: is blocked
concepts.gloss: All channels carried through the affected WSS input or unit are prevented from passing at that location.
concepts.example: A failed WSS input blocks the complete wavelength set arriving on one ROADM degree.

concepts.label: are unaffected
concepts.gloss: Channels outside the directly affected input, path, or component continue operating without the stated defect.
concepts.example: When one WSS input fails, channels entering on the ROADM's other degrees remain in service.

concepts.label: no light reaches the receiver
synonyms: No light at the line receiver.
no light arrives at the input of the receiving end of the multiplex section
concepts.gloss: No detectable optical light arrives at the line receiver, leading to declared loss of signal and loss of OTU frame alignment.
concepts.example: A fibre cut leaves the receiver input dark, so dLOS and OTU_LOF are declared.

concepts.label: declares loss of signal (G.798 dLOS)
concepts.gloss: The receiver asserts the G.798 optical loss-of-signal defect because received light is absent or below the detection criterion.
concepts.example: With receiver power below its LOS threshold, the unit declares dLOS and raises OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: frame alignment is lost
synonyms: OTU frame alignment lost while light is present.
concepts.gloss: The receiver cannot recover OTU frame boundaries, whether light is absent or too impaired, and consequently inserts ODU-AIS downstream and sends backward defect indication upstream.
concepts.example: Severe OSNR degradation leaves light present but causes OTU_LOF, ODU-AIS insertion, and OTU-BDI toward the transmitter.

concepts.label: Card hardware fault.
concepts.gloss: An internal hardware defect of a card that causes an equipment defect, loss of traffic framing, and masking of derivative traffic alarms.
concepts.example: A processor failure on a VB-OTN-LC-400 raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL and suppresses its secondary traffic alarms.

concepts.label: declares an equipment defect (dEQ)
concepts.gloss: The unit asserts the equipment-defect indication dEQ after detecting an internal hardware failure.
concepts.example: A failed line-card subsystem causes the card to declare dEQ.

concepts.label: the unit's traffic alarms are masked by the equipment alarm
synonyms: are masked by the equipment alarm
concepts.gloss: Traffic-related alarms from a failed unit are suppressed or subordinated because its equipment alarm already identifies the primary fault.
concepts.example: EQPT_CARD_FAIL remains visible while consequent LOS and framing alarms from that card are masked.

concepts.label: lower power, a lower signal-to-noise ratio, a raised differential group delay, a filtering penalty from a misaligned or narrowed passband, a receiver-side penalty, or a slow loss of margin
concepts.gloss: A composite class of optical or receiver impairments—including low power, poor SNR, high DGD, filtering penalty, receiver penalty, or gradual margin loss—that first raises pre-FEC errors and can progress to frame loss.
concepts.example: A narrowing ROADM passband initially causes OTU_SD and, as the penalty worsens, eventually causes OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: pre-FEC errors appear
synonyms: Signal degraded: pre-FEC errors above threshold
concepts.gloss: The line receiver observes a pre-forward-error-correction error rate above the degradation criterion, localized to that receiver.
concepts.example: A receiver records pre-FEC BER of 2×10⁻³ and raises the minor OTU_SD alarm.

concepts.label: Polarisation changes faster than the tracking range
concepts.gloss: The incoming signal's polarization changes more rapidly than the coherent receiver can track, resulting in errored seconds.
concepts.example: A fast fibre polarization transient exceeds the DSP tracking rate and creates several errored seconds.

concepts.label: produce errored seconds
concepts.gloss: The impairment causes one or more monitored one-second intervals to contain transmission errors.
concepts.example: A polarization transient causes five client errored seconds in the current 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: an ODU alarm indication signal
synonyms: an ODU alarm indication signal is inserted downstream
carries an ODU alarm indication signal onwards on every ODU cross-connected through it
an alarm indication signal is carried onwards
An ODU alarm indication signal is received.
concepts.gloss: An ODU-AIS maintenance signal is received or inserted and carried onward for affected ODUs to indicate an upstream server-layer defect, resulting in client-service failure.
concepts.example: After OTU frame loss, the unit inserts ODU-AIS on each carried ODU and the downstream client port reports ODU_AIS.

concepts.label: a backward defect indication is sent
concepts.gloss: A backward defect indication is transmitted toward the far-end source to report that the forward OTU signal is defective.
concepts.example: On losing OTU frame alignment, the receiver sends BDI upstream and the transmitting end reports OTU_BDI.

concepts.label: loses the signal
concepts.gloss: The far-end receiver no longer receives the optical channel transmitted by the affected source.
concepts.example: When the local transmit laser fails, the remote line receiver loses that wavelength.

concepts.label: The client service has failed.
concepts.gloss: The client-facing traffic service is unavailable or interrupted for the applicable channel, port, optic, unit traffic, or ODU set at the indicated endpoint or downstream location.
concepts.example: A switch-fabric failure interrupts every ODU through the switch and each associated client port raises CLIENT_SF.

concepts.label: goes silent
concepts.gloss: The affected equipment ceases providing its normal monitoring or telemetry output.
concepts.example: After a remote card failure, its performance counters stop updating.

concepts.label: are normal
concepts.gloss: Other channels outside the affected receiver or path retain normal operating measurements and service.
concepts.example: One receiver shows high pre-FEC BER while all neighbouring channels remain normal.

concepts.label: is normal
concepts.gloss: The optical path's externally observed state is normal, indicating that a detected impairment is local to the receiver rather than the path.
concepts.example: Channel power and OSNR along the path are nominal even though this receiver reports errors.

concepts.label: The far end reports a defect on the signal this unit transmits.
concepts.gloss: The remote endpoint has returned a backward defect report for the OTU signal transmitted by the current unit.
concepts.example: The local transmitter receives BDI after the far-end receiver loses frame alignment and reports OTU_BDI.

concepts.label: The unit has detected a fault in its transmit laser.
concepts.gloss: The current unit's internal diagnostics have identified a hardware fault in its own transmit laser.
concepts.example: Laser bias monitoring detects a failed transmitter and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL on the unit.

concepts.label: All three units operate
concepts.gloss: All three amplifier units in the referenced arrangement are operational, allowing the system to maintain constant-gain control.
concepts.example: The booster, inline amplifier, and preamplifier are all healthy, so the chain runs in constant-gain mode.

concepts.label: constant-gain mode
concepts.gloss: An amplifier operating mode in which control adjusts the pump to maintain a configured optical gain despite input-power variation.
concepts.example: The line amplifier increases pump drive after input power falls so that its gain remains at 20 dB.

concepts.label: the input is weak
synonyms: less light arrives at the input
concepts.gloss: The total optical signal arriving at an amplifier input is below its expected level, leading to weak output and a residual SNR penalty.
concepts.example: Only -25 dBm total power reaches the inline amplifier instead of -18 dBm, so its output is also weak.

concepts.label: the output is weak
concepts.gloss: The total output of an optical unit is below its expected power, affecting every channel that the unit carries.
concepts.example: A gain-degraded amplifier emits 4 dB below target across all wavelengths.

concepts.label: Loss of the OSC on one section
synonyms: the supervisory channel is not received
concepts.gloss: The optical supervisory channel is not received across one fibre section, while the defect is section-local and does not automatically propagate to the following section.
concepts.example: An inline amplifier loses the incoming OSC and raises OSC_LOS, but regenerates the management channel for the next span.

concepts.label: does not propagate to the next
concepts.gloss: A section-level defect terminates at the receiving node rather than being forwarded as the same defect onto the next section.
concepts.example: OSC loss is reported on span A–B, while the OSC on span B–C remains present.

concepts.label: no light arrives
synonyms: no light arrives at its input
concepts.gloss: An optical amplifier or unit receives no detectable light at its input, so no traffic light can leave its output.
concepts.example: A fibre break ahead of an inline amplifier leaves its input dark and causes AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: no light leaves
concepts.gloss: The unit's optical output is dark, either because it received no light or because the unit itself failed.
concepts.example: A failed pump leaves the line amplifier output at no detectable power.

concepts.label: light is present at its input but none leaves its output
concepts.gloss: Input light is detectable at an amplifier but its output is dark, distinguishing an internal amplifier failure from an upstream loss of input.
concepts.example: The preamplifier measures -18 dBm at its input and no output light, so it raises AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: raises its drive current to hold the gain
concepts.gloss: An ageing amplifier compensates by increasing pump-laser drive current so that configured gain remains stable.
concepts.example: The controller raises pump current from 100% to 112% of beginning-of-life current while maintaining 20 dB gain.

concepts.label: Traffic is unaffected until the drive current reaches its limit
concepts.gloss: All traffic through the amplifier remains serviceable while pump-current headroom still permits gain compensation, but becomes vulnerable once the drive limit is reached.
concepts.example: Channels remain error-free at 115% pump current, although further ageing will exhaust the control range.

concepts.label: gives early warning
concepts.gloss: A monitored trend exposes a developing equipment problem before it causes a traffic outage.
concepts.example: A month-by-month rise in normalized pump current warns operations of pump ageing while services remain unaffected.

concepts.label: leads eventually to the end-of-life alarm (AMP_PUMP_EOL)
concepts.gloss: Continuation of the monitored pump-health trend eventually crosses the threshold that raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.
concepts.example: Normalized pump current climbs past 120%, causing the minor AMP_PUMP_EOL alarm.

concepts.label: arrive weaker than the others
concepts.gloss: Only a subset of channels, often those near one edge of the optical band, have lower received power than the remaining channels.
concepts.example: The three highest-frequency wavelengths arrive 2 dB weaker than the centre-band wavelengths because of gain tilt.

concepts.label: the gain departs from its set point by more than 2 dB
concepts.gloss: An amplifier's measured gain differs from its configured target by more than 2 dB, satisfying the out-of-range alarm criterion.
concepts.example: Measured gain falls to 17.6 dB against a 20 dB set point, raising AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: the pump drive current exceeds 120 per cent of its beginning-of-life value
concepts.gloss: The amplifier pump requires more than 120% of its beginning-of-life drive current, meeting the vendor's pump end-of-life criterion.
concepts.example: A pump originally requiring 500 mA now requires 610 mA, or 122%, and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: Trail trace identifier mismatch: the ODU received is not the one expected.
synonyms: an ODU delivered from the wrong source
concepts.gloss: The received ODU trail trace identifier differs from the provisioned expected identifier, indicating delivery from the wrong source and causing service failure.
concepts.example: A port expecting trace CLIENT_A receives CLIENT_B after a bad cross-connect and raises ODU_TIM.

concepts.label: the service is protected
concepts.gloss: The client service has a protection arrangement with an alternate ODU path available for recovery from a path defect.
concepts.example: A service is provisioned over separate working and protection ODU paths.

concepts.label: the selector can choose a path free of defects
concepts.gloss: At least one protected ODU path is defect-free and can be selected to continue the service.
concepts.example: When the working path fails but the protection path is healthy, the selector switches to protection.

concepts.label: the service suffers only a brief hit while the selector switches
concepts.gloss: A protected service experiences only a short traffic interruption during selector switchover rather than a sustained outage.
concepts.example: A working-path cut causes a 40 ms interruption before traffic resumes on the protection path.

concepts.label: is delivered to the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: A single ODU is switched to an unintended endpoint because its cross-connection is incorrect.
concepts.example: The ODU for site A emerges at site B after an erroneous fabric mapping.

concepts.label: There is no optical symptom.
concepts.gloss: The misrouted ODU has normal underlying optical power and framing, so the fault is visible only at the digital service or trail level.
concepts.example: Channel power and OTU framing remain normal while ODU_TIM reveals that the payload came from the wrong source.

concepts.label: The far end reports that it is receiving an alarm indication signal.
concepts.gloss: The remote endpoint reports via ODU backward defect indication that the signal it receives contains an alarm indication signal.
concepts.example: A downstream client port receives ODU-AIS and sends BDI, causing the source-side port to report ODU_BDI.

concepts.label: The selector is on the protection path.
concepts.gloss: The protection selector is currently forwarding traffic from the protection ODU path instead of the working path.
concepts.example: After a working-path defect, the client port selects the protection leg and raises PROT_ACTIVE.

concepts.label: The protection path has failed.
concepts.gloss: The standby protection ODU path is defective or unavailable, leaving the protected service without a usable alternate path.
concepts.example: Traffic remains on a healthy working path, but a cut on the standby leg raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

concepts.label: Port hardware fault.
concepts.gloss: An internal hardware defect of a client port that prevents reliable operation of that port.
concepts.example: A failed 100GE port PHY causes EQPT_PORT_FAIL on the affected client port.

concepts.label: Fabric fault.
concepts.gloss: An internal hardware or functional defect in an OTN switch's ODU cross-connect fabric.
concepts.example: The VB-OTNSW detects a failed switching-fabric plane and raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

concepts.label: the power of every channel
concepts.gloss: A per-wavelength measurement of optical power for each channel, available where the node has the channel-monitoring option.
concepts.example: A channel monitor reports -9.8 dBm for 193.1 THz and -10.4 dBm for 193.2 THz.

concepts.label: the OSNR of every channel
concepts.gloss: An estimated optical signal-to-noise ratio for each wavelength, provided by channel-monitoring or advanced-monitoring capabilities.
concepts.example: The node estimates OSNRs of 19.5 dB and 17.2 dB for two routed channels.

concepts.label: Received power
concepts.gloss: The optical power measured at a unit's receiver or receive interface, supported generally or through the applicable power-monitoring option.
concepts.example: A transponder reports received channel power of -13.2 dBm.

concepts.label: errored seconds, in 15-minute bins
concepts.gloss: A performance counter recording how many seconds contained client errors during each 15-minute measurement interval.
concepts.example: A client port reports 12 errored seconds for the 10:00–10:15 bin.

concepts.label: pre-FEC bit error ratio
concepts.gloss: The bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction, used to quantify received line-signal quality on units with advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: A coherent receiver reports a pre-FEC BER of 8×10⁻⁴.

concepts.label: differential group delay
concepts.gloss: The measured propagation-time difference between principal polarization modes of the received optical signal.
concepts.example: Advanced monitoring reports 18 ps of differential group delay on the channel.

concepts.label: polarisation change rate
concepts.gloss: The measured rate at which the received signal's state of polarization changes over time.
concepts.example: The receiver records a polarization change rate that spikes above its normal tracking range during fibre work.

concepts.label: Total optical power at the unit's input
concepts.gloss: The aggregate optical power of all wavelengths measured at an amplifier unit's input.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-ILA reports total input power of -18 dBm.

concepts.label: Total optical power at the unit's output
concepts.gloss: The aggregate optical power of all wavelengths measured at an amplifier unit's output.
concepts.example: The same VB-OA-ILA reports total output power of +2 dBm.

concepts.label: Drive current of the pump laser, as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value
concepts.gloss: The amplifier pump-laser drive current normalized to its beginning-of-life value, used as an indicator of pump ageing and health.
concepts.example: Advanced monitoring reports pump drive at 118% of its beginning-of-life current.

concepts.label: Presence of the supervisory channel at the input
concepts.gloss: A binary or status measurement indicating whether the optical supervisory channel is detected at the amplifier input.
concepts.example: A line amplifier reports OSC absent on its incoming fibre section.

concepts.label: client unavailable seconds
concepts.gloss: A client-port performance counter recording seconds during which the client service was unavailable, accumulated in 15-minute bins.
concepts.example: A port records 90 unavailable seconds in the current 15-minute interval.

concepts.label: ROADM
concepts.gloss: A reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexer, here specifically a colourless, directionless and contentionless device that independently routes wavelength channels.
concepts.example: VB-ROADM-CDC switches a 193.1 THz channel from an incoming degree to a selected outgoing degree.

concepts.label: Transponder
concepts.gloss: An optical transport unit that maps a client signal to and from a single line-side wavelength.
concepts.example: VB-TPD-400 carries a 400GE client over one coherent optical channel.

concepts.label: Muxponder
concepts.gloss: An optical transport unit that multiplexes multiple lower-rate client signals into a higher-rate line signal and demultiplexes them on receive.
concepts.example: VB-MXP-400 aggregates four 100GE clients onto a 400G line channel.

concepts.label: OTN line card
concepts.gloss: A card providing OTN line-side termination and transport functions at its supported capacity.
concepts.example: VB-OTN-LC-400 terminates a 400G OTU and exposes its carried ODUs to the switch.

concepts.label: All units
concepts.gloss: The collective class of VB transponders, muxponders, and OTN line cards that measure received power and 15-minute errored-second performance.
concepts.example: A VB-TPD-400, VB-MXP-400, and VB-OTN-LC-400 can each report received power and errored seconds.

concepts.label: Booster amplifier (BA)
synonyms: At the transmitting end of a multiplex section, after the ROADM
concepts.gloss: An optical amplifier placed after the ROADM at the transmitting end of a multiplex section to raise launch power and monitor input, output, pump health, and OSC presence.
concepts.example: VB-OA-BST boosts the multiplex leaving a ROADM before it enters the fibre span.

concepts.label: Line amplifier (LA)
concepts.gloss: An intermediate-site optical amplifier that restores multiplex power between terminal nodes and monitors optical power, pump drive, and OSC presence.
concepts.example: VB-OA-ILA amplifies all wavelengths midway along a long-haul span.

concepts.label: Preamplifier (PA)
synonyms: At the receiving end of a multiplex section, before the ROADM
concepts.gloss: An optical amplifier placed before the ROADM at the receiving end of a multiplex section to raise incoming multiplex power and provide amplifier monitoring.
concepts.example: VB-OA-PRE amplifies a weak incoming line before channel demultiplexing at the ROADM.

concepts.label: OTN switch
concepts.gloss: An OTN device whose fabric cross-connects ODU containers between ports and paths.
concepts.example: VB-OTNSW switches an ODU4 from an ingress line card to a 100GE client egress.

concepts.label: Client port, 10GE
concepts.gloss: A client-facing port resource supporting a 10 Gigabit Ethernet service interface.
concepts.example: VB-CP-10GE terminates a customer's 10GE connection.

concepts.label: Client port, 100GE
concepts.gloss: A client-facing port resource supporting a 100 Gigabit Ethernet service interface.
concepts.example: VB-CP-100GE accepts a 100GE router link for OTN transport.

concepts.label: Client port, 400GE
concepts.gloss: A client-facing port resource supporting a 400 Gigabit Ethernet service interface.
concepts.example: VB-CP-400GE connects a 400GE client to a coherent transponder.

concepts.label: client port
concepts.gloss: The generic client-facing service interface that measures client errored seconds and unavailable seconds.
concepts.example: A 100GE client port reports three errored seconds and zero unavailable seconds in a 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: OCH_LOS
concepts.gloss: A critical optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm raised by a line-terminating unit when no light reaches its line receiver, with likely causes along the source or optical path.
concepts.example: A fibre cut removes receiver light and a VB-TPD-400 raises OCH_LOS against its line receiver.

concepts.label: OTU_LOF
concepts.gloss: A critical OTU loss-of-frame alarm raised when a line unit cannot recover OTU frame alignment because the present signal is absent or severely impaired.
concepts.example: Severe OSNR degradation from amplifier noise causes a VB-OTN-LC-400 to raise OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: OTU_SD
concepts.gloss: A minor OTU signal-degrade alarm raised when line-receiver pre-FEC errors exceed the configured degradation threshold.
concepts.example: A dirty connector raises pre-FEC BER above threshold and the unit reports OTU_SD.

concepts.label: OTU_BDI
concepts.gloss: A non-alarming OTU backward-defect indication status showing that the far end reports a defect on the OTU signal transmitted by this unit.
concepts.example: The remote receiver loses frame alignment and sends BDI, so the local unit records OTU_BDI.

concepts.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical equipment alarm raised by a transport unit when it detects failure of its own transmit laser.
concepts.example: A VB-MXP-400 detects zero laser output and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL against itself.

concepts.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical equipment alarm raised by a transport unit for a hardware failure of its card.
concepts.example: A VB-OTN-LC-200 suffers an internal hardware fault and raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL against the card.

concepts.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
concepts.gloss: A critical line-amplifier alarm indicating that no optical traffic light is arriving at its input, usually because of upstream fibre loss or amplifier failure.
concepts.example: A span cut leaves a VB-OA-ILA input dark and it raises AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: OMS_LOS_P
concepts.gloss: A critical optical multiplex section loss-of-signal alarm raised by a preamplifier when no line light reaches the receiving end.
concepts.example: A disconnected receive-side patch cord causes VB-OA-PRE to raise OMS_LOS_P.

concepts.label: OSC_LOS
concepts.gloss: A major section alarm raised by a line amplifier or preamplifier when the incoming optical supervisory channel is absent on its feeding fibre section.
concepts.example: Excess span loss removes the OSC at a VB-OA-ILA, which raises OSC_LOS against that fibre section.

concepts.label: AMP_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical amplifier alarm raised when input light is present but the booster, line amplifier, or preamplifier produces no output, indicating internal unit or pump failure.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-BST sees valid input power but no output after pump failure and raises AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
concepts.gloss: A minor line-amplifier or preamplifier alarm indicating measured gain differs from its set point by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-PRE set to 20 dB measures 17.5 dB and raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
concepts.gloss: A minor amplifier pump end-of-life alarm raised when normalized pump drive current exceeds 120% because of pump ageing.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-ILA reaches 123% of beginning-of-life pump current and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: CLIENT_SF
concepts.gloss: A critical client-port service-failure alarm indicating loss of the associated client service due to a port, path, cross-connection, or switch-fabric fault.
concepts.example: A failed 100GE client port raises CLIENT_SF on that port.

concepts.label: ODU_AIS
concepts.gloss: A non-alarming client-port status indicating receipt of an ODU alarm indication signal generated by an upstream server-layer failure.
concepts.example: After upstream OTU_LOF, the downstream client port receives ODU-AIS and reports ODU_AIS.

concepts.label: ODU_BDI
concepts.gloss: A non-alarming client-port status indicating that the far end reports receipt of an ODU alarm indication signal.
concepts.example: A remote port receiving ODU-AIS returns BDI, so the local client port reports ODU_BDI.

concepts.label: ODU_TIM
concepts.gloss: A major client-port alarm raised when the received ODU trail trace does not match the expected source, commonly due to a wrong cross-connection.
concepts.example: A port provisioned for CLIENT_A receives CLIENT_B's trail trace and raises ODU_TIM.

concepts.label: PROT_ACTIVE
concepts.gloss: A minor client-port status indicating that protection switching has selected the protection ODU path, typically because the working path failed.
concepts.example: A working-path fibre fault causes the selector to move to protection and raise PROT_ACTIVE.

concepts.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
concepts.gloss: A minor client-port alarm indicating that the protection ODU path has failed and is unavailable as a standby route.
concepts.example: The service remains on its working path while a defect on the protection path raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

concepts.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical client-port equipment alarm indicating a hardware fault in that port.
concepts.example: A failed Ethernet PHY on VB-CP-100GE raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

concepts.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical alarm raised by an OTN switch when its ODU cross-connect fabric has an internal fault.
concepts.example: VB-OTNSW detects a fabric-plane failure and raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

concepts.label: The channel
concepts.gloss: The single optical wavelength channel directly associated with the stated signal, condition, or service.
concepts.example: Low power caused by WSS attenuation drift applies only to the affected 193.1 THz channel.

concepts.label: Every channel carried by the unit
synonyms: Every channel arriving at the node on that degree
concepts.gloss: The complete set of wavelength channels or traffic streams passing through the affected unit or incoming degree.
concepts.example: An amplifier output failure interrupts all 80 channels carried by that amplifier.

concepts.label: other channels
synonyms: channels arriving on the other degrees
concepts.gloss: Channels outside the specifically affected channel, receiver, or ROADM degree that serve as unaffected comparison traffic.
concepts.example: A WSS input fault blocks one degree while channels arriving on the other degrees continue normally.

concepts.label: Some channels, not all
synonyms: channels at one edge of the band
concepts.gloss: A proper subset of the carried channels, often channels near one spectral-band edge rather than the full multiplex.
concepts.example: Gain tilt weakens the top eight wavelengths but not the other 72.

concepts.label: the traffic it receives
concepts.gloss: The client or transport traffic presented to and handled by the referenced unit or endpoint.
concepts.example: A failed far-end card loses all traffic that it receives from its local client.

concepts.label: its monitoring
concepts.gloss: The telemetry, performance data, and status reporting produced by the referenced unit.
concepts.example: When a card goes silent, its counters and status updates stop while monitoring is affected.

concepts.label: its traffic alarms
concepts.gloss: The set of service- and signal-related alarms generated by the referenced unit, excluding its primary equipment alarm.
concepts.example: A card hardware alarm masks that card's derivative LOS and frame alarms.

concepts.label: this receiver only
concepts.gloss: The local receiver under diagnosis, excluding other receivers and channels on the same optical path.
concepts.example: Pre-FEC errors appear on one transponder receiver while neighbouring receivers remain normal.

concepts.label: the optical path
concepts.gloss: The end-to-end optical route traversed by the channel, including fibre, amplifiers, connectors, and ROADMs.
concepts.example: Path power and OSNR are normal from transmitter to receiver, pointing to a local receiver defect.

concepts.label: the unit
concepts.gloss: The particular managed hardware unit whose state or output is being described.
concepts.example: No light leaves the affected line-amplifier unit.

concepts.label: the trend
concepts.gloss: The time series of a monitored value used to identify gradual change or predict a threshold crossing.
concepts.example: The upward trend in normalized pump current provides early warning of pump ageing.

concepts.label: Every ODU cross-connected through the switch
concepts.gloss: All ODU containers whose routes traverse the affected OTN switch fabric.
concepts.example: A fabric failure inserts ODU-AIS into every ODU crossing that switch.

concepts.label: one ODU
concepts.gloss: A single Optical Data Unit trail or container, rather than every ODU on the link or switch.
concepts.example: A wrong cross-connect misroutes one ODU4 while other ODUs remain correctly mapped.

concepts.label: The client optic
concepts.gloss: The optical transceiver on the client-facing side of a port.
concepts.example: A local client-optic failure interrupts the connected 100GE service.

concepts.label: the port
concepts.gloss: The individual physical or logical client interface to which the condition applies.
concepts.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL affects one 400GE port, not the whole line card.

concepts.label: the client service
concepts.gloss: The end-user traffic service carried through the client interface and transport network.
concepts.example: A 100GE customer circuit is unavailable after its client port fails.

concepts.label: downstream
concepts.gloss: At nodes, links, or receivers later in the traffic direction than the referenced point.
concepts.example: Low channel power introduced at a ROADM is observed at the next downstream amplifier.

concepts.label: there
concepts.gloss: At the fault location or component just identified by the surrounding diagnostic context.
concepts.example: All channels are blocked there at the failed WSS input port.

concepts.label: The receiver at the far end
concepts.gloss: The line receiver at the endpoint opposite the transmitting unit across the channel.
concepts.example: Failure of the local laser is observed as signal loss at the receiver at the far end.

concepts.label: the far end
concepts.gloss: The remote endpoint of the monitored service or transport connection relative to the current unit.
concepts.example: A remote card failure causes the client service to fail at the far end.

concepts.label: here
concepts.gloss: The local endpoint or currently observed node, as opposed to the remote far end.
concepts.example: A remote transmission failure is manifested here as loss of incoming client traffic.

concepts.label: the line receiver
concepts.gloss: The local line-side optical receiver that terminates the incoming wavelength or OTU signal.
concepts.example: OCH_LOS is reported against the line receiver when no light is detected.

concepts.label: the far-end transmitter
concepts.gloss: The remote line transmitter that sends the optical signal received by the current unit.
concepts.example: A transmit-laser fault at the far-end transmitter causes local OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: along the channel's path
synonyms: on the path to the far end
concepts.gloss: At an unspecified component or span on the end-to-end route followed by the optical channel.
concepts.example: A dirty connector at an intermediate patch panel lies along the channel's path.

concepts.label: the signal this unit transmits
concepts.gloss: The outbound OTU or optical signal generated by the current unit and evaluated through far-end defect feedback.
concepts.example: OTU_BDI is reported against the signal this unit transmits after the remote receiver detects a defect.

concepts.label: this unit
concepts.gloss: Within or on the currently managed hardware unit rather than elsewhere in the network.
concepts.example: EQPT_TX_FAIL identifies a failed laser in this unit.

concepts.label: this card
concepts.gloss: Within or on the particular equipment card currently being managed.
concepts.example: EQPT_CARD_FAIL is reported against this VB-OTN-LC-400 card.

concepts.label: the output
concepts.gloss: The egress optical interface of the referenced unit, where emitted power or absence of light is observed.
concepts.example: After pump failure, no light is measured at the amplifier output.

concepts.label: the fibre section feeding this unit
synonyms: the fibre section feeding the unit, not against the unit itself
concepts.gloss: The incoming fibre span immediately upstream of the unit, treated separately from the unit itself.
concepts.example: OSC_LOS is assigned to the fibre section feeding the line amplifier after a span cut.

concepts.label: the preceding amplifier
concepts.gloss: The nearest upstream optical amplifier whose output feeds the current span or unit.
concepts.example: No light reaches the current amplifier because the preceding amplifier has failed.

concepts.label: at the input of the multiplex section
concepts.gloss: At the transmitting-side entry point where optical traffic is launched into a multiplex section.
concepts.example: A disconnected patch cord at the multiplex-section input removes all launched wavelengths.

concepts.label: through the switch
concepts.gloss: Within the ODU forwarding route across an OTN switch's cross-connect fabric.
concepts.example: Every service routed through the failed switch fabric is interrupted.

concepts.label: the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: An unintended endpoint to which an incorrectly cross-connected ODU has been delivered.
concepts.example: The ODU intended for site A appears at site B, the wrong destination.

concepts.label: on the ODU path currently in use
concepts.gloss: At some point on whichever working or protection ODU route the selector is presently using for service traffic.
concepts.example: A defect on the currently selected protection path interrupts the service even though the working path is idle.

concepts.label: at either end
concepts.gloss: At either the local endpoint or the remote endpoint of the client service.
concepts.example: A client-port failure can occur here on the local port or at the far-end port.

concepts.label: in an OTN switch along the ODU path
concepts.gloss: Inside an OTN switch traversed by the ODU trail, particularly its cross-connect configuration or fabric.
concepts.example: A wrong cross-connection in an intermediate VB-OTNSW sends the ODU to the wrong egress.

concepts.label: client port
concepts.gloss: At the client-facing interface where service, ODU, protection, or equipment status is reported.
concepts.example: ODU_TIM is reported against the 100GE client port.

concepts.label: on the working ODU path
concepts.gloss: At a component or link belonging to the primary ODU route used under normal conditions.
concepts.example: A fibre fault on the working ODU path triggers a switch to protection.

concepts.label: on the protection ODU path
concepts.gloss: At a component or link belonging to the alternate ODU route reserved for protection.
concepts.example: A defect on the protection ODU path raises PROT_UNAVAIL while working traffic continues.

concepts.label: this port
concepts.gloss: Within or on the specific currently managed interface rather than elsewhere on the service path.
concepts.example: A hardware failure on this port raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

concepts.label: this switch's fabric
concepts.gloss: Within the internal ODU cross-connect fabric of the currently managed OTN switch.
concepts.example: A failed fabric plane in this switch causes OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

concepts.label: available on nodes with the channel monitoring option
concepts.gloss: The measurement is exposed only on nodes equipped and licensed with the channel-monitoring option.
concepts.example: A ROADM with channel monitoring reports per-channel power, while a node without the option does not.

concepts.label: All units
concepts.gloss: The measurement or function is supported by every transponder, muxponder, and OTN line-card unit in the defined VB unit class.
concepts.example: Every VB-TPD-400, VB-MXP-200, and VB-OTN-LC-400 reports received power.

concepts.label: Units with the power monitoring option
concepts.gloss: The measurement is available only on units fitted or licensed for optical power monitoring.
concepts.example: A power-monitoring-enabled VB-OA-ILA reports total input and output power.

concepts.label: Units with the advanced monitoring option
concepts.gloss: The measurement is available only on units with the advanced optical or signal monitoring capability.
concepts.example: An advanced-monitoring transponder reports estimated OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, and polarization change rate.

concepts.label: Each client port reports client errored seconds in 15-minute bins.
synonyms: Each client port reports client unavailable seconds in 15-minute bins.
concepts.gloss: Every client port supplies 15-minute performance bins for client errored seconds and client unavailable seconds.
concepts.example: A VB-CP-100GE reports 7 errored seconds and 30 unavailable seconds for the last 15-minute interval.

concepts.label: A degradation
synonyms: gradual or step degradation rather than an outage
concepts.gloss: A non-outage impairment in which signal or equipment performance worsens but some traffic or optical signal remains present.
concepts.example: A shifted WSS passband leaves the channel present but increases pre-FEC errors.

concepts.label: Hard failure
concepts.gloss: An abrupt, service-affecting loss of a component's required function rather than a gradual reduction in performance.
concepts.example: A transmit laser stops emitting completely and the remote receiver loses signal.

concepts.label: slow, incipient condition
concepts.gloss: A gradually developing condition detectable by trend monitoring before it reaches a service-affecting failure threshold.
concepts.example: Pump drive rises over several months while gain and traffic remain stable.

concepts.label: mostly just after provisioning changes
concepts.gloss: A fault pattern primarily associated with recent configuration or cross-connection changes rather than spontaneous physical degradation.
concepts.example: Immediately after an ODU reroute, an incorrect mapping delivers the service to the wrong port.

concepts.label: critical
concepts.gloss: The highest listed alarm severity, assigned to faults that cause or imminently represent major loss of equipment function or traffic.
concepts.example: OCH_LOS is marked critical when no light reaches the line receiver.

concepts.label: minor
concepts.gloss: A lower alarm severity used for degradations, warnings, or protection states that do not necessarily represent an immediate sustained outage.
concepts.example: AMP_PUMP_EOL is minor because it warns of ageing while gain and traffic may still be maintained.

concepts.label: not alarmed
concepts.gloss: A reported defect or maintenance indication retained as status information without contributing an active alarm severity.
concepts.example: ODU_AIS is recorded as not alarmed because it is a consequent indication of an upstream fault.

concepts.label: major
concepts.gloss: A serious alarm severity below critical, used for substantial defects requiring action but not classified as immediate critical equipment or traffic loss.
concepts.example: ODU_TIM is major because the service is sourced from the wrong ODU despite normal optics.

concepts.label: Each channel leaving a degree is switched separately.
concepts.gloss: A ROADM independently controls the switching of each wavelength exiting a degree, so a channel-specific route or block need not affect other wavelengths.
concepts.example: The ROADM directs 193.1 THz east and 193.2 THz south while leaving the remaining channels on their existing routes.

concepts.label: When frame alignment is lost, the unit applies the G.798 consequent actions: an ODU alarm indication signal is inserted downstream on every ODU the OTU carries, and a backward defect indication is sent to the far-end transmitter.
concepts.gloss: On OTU frame-alignment loss, the unit performs G.798 consequent actions by inserting ODU-AIS downstream on every carried ODU and transmitting BDI toward the far-end transmitter.
concepts.example: OTU_LOF on a line card causes all of its mapped ODUs to carry AIS while the remote source receives OTU_BDI.

concepts.label: The OTN switch carries an ODU alarm indication signal onwards on every ODU cross-connected through it.
concepts.gloss: An OTN switch transparently forwards an incoming ODU alarm indication signal on every affected ODU cross-connected through its fabric.
concepts.example: ODU-AIS entering VB-OTNSW on an ODU4 remains present when that ODU4 exits toward the client port.
